subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram DMs can still land in agent:main:main, polluting heartbeat/main session after #40519

question: Should maintainers split the remaining work so `heartbeat.session` precedence is fixed first while Telegram default DM isolation stays under the existing `session.dmScope` policy?
rationale: Current source proves a heartbeat precedence bug, but silently changing Telegram DMs away from the documented main-session default was already rejected as a product-policy shift and would affect existing users.

options.title: Split heartbeat fix first
options.body: Adopt, repair, or replace the heartbeat wake/session repair so configured heartbeat sessions win, while leaving default Telegram DM isolation controlled by the documented `session.dmScope` policy.

options.title: Change Telegram DM defaults
options.body: Reopen the cross-channel product decision and update Telegram routing, docs, upgrade expectations, and tests so unset Telegram DMs isolate by default.

options.title: Defer to native heartbeat entries
options.body: Hold this behind the broader native per-session heartbeat scheduling design, accepting that the current event-wake precedence path remains unresolved for now.

recommendation.title: Split heartbeat fix first
recommendation.body: Adopt, repair, or replace the heartbeat wake/session repair so configured heartbeat sessions win, while leaving default Telegram DM isolation controlled by the documented `session.dmScope` policy.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus made the prior product-policy call on Telegram DM default isolation and authored the adjacent duplicate-reply fix that scoped itself away from session selection.
